title: How to choose the best cash management accounts offered by brokerages
description: Replacing your traditional bank with a high-yield fintech hybrid.
content:
The line between 'Bank' and 'Brokerage' has blurred. Today, brokerages like Fidelity, Schwab, and Wealthfront offer 'Cash Management Accounts' (CMAs) that function like checking accounts but pay interest rates like savings accounts. For many Americans, the CMA is the superior hub for their financial life—offering FDIC insurance, debit cards, bill pay, and 5.0% APY all in one place. This guide explains how to break up with your low-interest bank and consolidate your finances.

Key Takeaways

  • High Yield Checking: Traditional checking pays 0.01%. CMAs often pay 4-5% by sweeping cash into partner banks or money market funds. On a $10k balance, that's $500/year found money.
  • FDIC Stacking: CMAs spread your cash across multiple program banks behind the scenes, offering up to $2 Million - $5 Million in FDIC insurance (vs $250k at a regular bank).
  • ATM Freedom: Fidelity and Schwab CMAs reimburse all ATM fees worldwide. You never have to look for a specific network machine again.
  • Overdraft Protection: CMAs link directly to your investment portfolio, allowing you to use margin (optional/risky) or secondary cash pools to cover accidental overdrafts freely.

Why It Matters (US Context)

The 'Cash Sweep' mechanism is unique to the US. Brokerages are not banks; they are intermediaries. They take your cash and deposit it at 'Program Banks' (like Citibank, HSBC) to get you FDIC coverage. You get the safety of a bank with the technology of a brokerage.

Top CMA Contenders

Which hybrid account wins?

1. Fidelity Cash Management

  • Yield: ~2.7% (FDIC Sweep) or ~5.0% (if you manually buy SPAXX). *Note: Fidelity recently allowed auto-sweep to SPAXX in CMAs.*
  • ATM Fees: Reimbursed globally.
  • Verdict: The King. Excellent for travel and yield.

2. Wealthfront Cash Account

  • Yield: ~5.0% (changes with Fed).
  • FDIC: Up to $8 Million (via network).
  • Features: Early direct deposit, bill pay.
  • Verdict: The best pure yield for a checking-replacement.

3. Charles Schwab Investor Checking

  • Yield: Low (~0.45%).
  • ATM Fees: Reimbursed globally. Best customer service.
  • Verdict: Best for travel and service, but you must manually move excess cash to a Money Market Fund (SWVXX) to get yield. Not automated.

The Consolidation Play

  1. Open the CMA: Open a Fidelity CMA. Order the debit card.
  2. Switch Direct Deposit: Move your payroll to the CMA. It is now your Hub.
  3. Link Bills: Set Auto-Pay for credit cards to pull from the CMA.
  4. The 'One Balance' Benefit: You no longer need to transfer money from Savings to Checking to pay a big bill. All your cash sits in one high-yield pool, accessible instantly. This eliminates 'Transfer friction'.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is it safe?

Yes. The cash is FDIC insured once it hits the program banks. SIPC protects securities. It is as safe as Chase or Wells Fargo.

Can I deposit cash?

This is the one weakness. Most CMAs have no physical branches. If you deal in paper cash often, keep a local Credit Union account for deposits, then transfer it to the CMA.

Does it have Zelle?

Chase/Wells own Zelle. Some brokerages (Schwab) have integrated it. Others (Wealthfront) have not. Check current feature lists if Zelle is critical to you.
